attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I've poured days of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-e6x6u4g_/call-3637ff6b942a44a4a783215ef0ee7c87/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(m, importlib.util.find_spec(m))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=page.extract_text()
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n'+t)
 (p/f'page-{i+1}.txt').write_text(t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "sed -n '1,320p' tmp/pdfs/page-16.txt && sed -n '1,320p' tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt && sed -n '1,360p' tmp/pdfs/page-18.txt && sed -n '1,320p' tmp/pdfs/page-19.txt && sed -n '1,320p' tmp/pdfs/page-20.txt"

strengths: The method addresses a valuable computer vision problem with a practical combination of feature matching and per-class BatchNorm regularization. Using a single pretrained teacher avoids expensive differentiation through student training and enables ImageNet-1K experiments.

Reported accuracy gains are substantial across several compression budgets. At 50 images per class, Table 1 reports 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5% for CDA, and 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus 48.7%. Repeated-run statistics strengthen this evidence.

The factorial ablation supports the combined design: with PCBN fixed, Wasserstein feature matching improves ImageNet-1K accuracy from 36.4% to 38.1%. Evaluation across three ResNets and two vision transformers provides useful evidence of transfer beyond the distillation architecture.

The pipeline is clearly illustrated, established methods and datasets are cited, and the supplement provides pseudocode and training settings. A code repository is linked, and Appendix A appropriately acknowledges the possibility of preserving source-dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central formulation has an unexamined equivalence to ordinary clustering. With one input distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized atom weights, Eqs. (5)–(8) reduce exactly to the k-means objective: minimizing the average squared distance to the nearest synthetic feature. This relationship is not discussed, and k-means targets under identical image optimization and PCBN are not evaluated. Consequently, the contribution beyond applying established feature quantization remains insufficiently distinguished.

Section 5.6 does not isolate the effect of the distance metric because the compared methods use different feature-extractor regimes. At one image per class, the Wasserstein target is exactly the class feature mean, making Eq. (12) equivalent to linear-MMD mean matching with the same encoder. Figure 4's 10.45% versus 0.48% therefore cannot establish a metric-specific advantage. Matched encoders, regularization, and optimization are needed. Appendix B appropriately qualifies its claims, but its generic risk bounds do not resolve this experimental confound.

Baseline comparability needs clarification. Table 1 reports 21.3% for SRe2L on ImageNet-1K at 10 images per class, whereas Table 4's SRe2L-style CE+BN configuration reaches 35.9%, much closer to WMDD's 38.1%. This unexplained difference materially changes the apparent improvement. The principal comparisons need clearly matched teacher, recovery, relabeling, and student-training settings.

Algorithm 2 updates the weights and then reuses a transport plan computed for the preceding weights, although Eq. (11) assumes that the plan's column sums equal the weights used in the update. Simplex projection can also produce zero weights, making division by those weights undefined. Coupling updates and zero-weight handling need clarification, alongside barycenter initialization, the step size, and the precise use of weights during FKD. These may be repairable description issues, but currently impede reproduction.

The efficiency evidence only partially supports the scalability claim. Table 3 compares methods on ImageNette at one image per class, and Table 5 supplies Tiny ImageNet timings. ImageNet-1K runtime and memory measurements, with clear accounting for teacher preparation, feature/statistic extraction, barycenter computation, and relabeling, are absent. The reported ImageNet results demonstrate feasibility, but comparative efficiency at that scale remains insufficiently established.
